title.en: US signs landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
title.zh: 美国将宣布允许沙特阿拉伯发展核计划的协议

summary.en: The United States is expected to announce an agreement that would permit Saudi Arabia to develop a nuclear program, a long-standing ambition for the kingdom. This potential deal has raised concerns in Israel and among some US lawmakers.
summary.zh: 美国预计将宣布一项协议，允许沙特阿拉伯发展核计划，这是沙特王国长期以来的愿望。这项潜在的协议引起了以色列和一些美国立法者的担忧。

body.en:
The US and Saudi Arabia have signed a landmark deal that will reportedly allow the Gulf kingdom to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

The deal is described as a "peaceful nuclear co-operation agreement" that will provide "great access for American companies in the Saudi nuclear energy program", according to a statement from the US energy secretary.

"Together, these two agreements lay the legal foundation for a decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership that advances several priority economic and strategic objectives, including nuclear nonproliferation," the statement reads.

Specific details were not given but earlier media reports , external suggested that, after undertaking a joint study with the US, Saudi Arabia may be allowed to enrich uranium on its soil to produce fuel at a US-built enrichment facility, instead of relying on imported fuel.

This could be worth billions of dollars to the US, whose companies could be involved in building a facility to produce enriched uranium, which can be used as fuel for power plants but also to make nuclear bombs.

According to Wednesday's statement, the deal will "advance US and regional security by upholding high standards of nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation and strengthening the United States' competitive edge in civil nuclear technology".

"Rest assured, these agreements uphold the highest standards of nuclear safety and nonproliferation, while relying on the world's best nuclear technology and scientists, designed right here in the United States," said US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright.

"Thanks to President Trump, the American nuclear renaissance is underway and will deliver long-term benefits to the American and Saudi people."

Nuclear experts and former officials in Israel - the US's top ally in the Middle East - voiced concern the plan could ultimately lead to Saudi Arabia being able to develop a nuclear weapon.

The agreement will now be sent to Congress for review. Some lawmakers on both sides of the political aisle are also expected to oppose the deal, though Trump's Republican Party controls both the upper and lower chambers.

The enrichment provision would distinguish this agreement from another one that was struck by the US in 2009 with Saudi Arabia's neighbour, the United Arab Emirates, under which the UAE does not produce its own fuel and accepts a host of other restrictions.

For that reason, the agreement is also expected to attract the concern of nuclear non-proliferation campaigners, whose ultimate aim is to prevent an increase in the number of nuclear weapons worldwide.

The US-Saudi deal has already been approved by Trump, according to The Wall Street Journal.

body.zh: 预计美国和沙特阿拉伯将宣布一项协议，允许海湾王国发展民用核计划。 据英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻报道，预计美国总统唐纳德·特朗普政府将于周三发布公告。 该协议对美国来说可能价值数十亿美元，美国公司可能参与建设浓缩铀生产设施，浓缩铀可用作发电厂的燃料，也可用于制造核弹。 美国在中东的顶级盟友以色列的核专家和前官员表示担心，该计划最终可能导致沙特阿拉伯能够发展核武器。 哥伦比亚广播公司援引一位熟悉该协议的地区官员的话说，该协议将允许美国公司在沙特领土上为沙特运营核电。所涉及的公司尚未披露，需要咨询国会。 据外部媒体报道，在与美国进行联合研究后，沙特阿拉伯可能被允许在其土地上浓缩铀，以在美国建造的浓缩设施中生产燃料，而不是依赖进口燃料。 据《华尔街日报》外部报道，这笔交易将持续 30 年，估计价值数百亿美元。 浓缩条款将使该协议与美国2009年与沙特阿拉伯邻国阿拉伯联合酋长国达成的另一项协议区分开来，根据该协议，阿联酋不生产自己的燃料，并接受一系列其他限制。 因此，该协议预计也会引起核不扩散活动人士的关注，他们的最终目标是防止全世界核武器数量的增加。 核问题一直是美以与伊朗长达数月冲突的核心。两国表示，他们二月份袭击伊朗的原因之一是为了阻止该国发展核武器——德黑兰否认有计划这样做。 沙特阿拉伯事实上的统治者、王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼在 2018 年告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，他自己的国家并不打算获得核武器，但“毫无疑问，如果伊朗研制出核弹，我们将尽快效仿”。 据《华尔街日报》报道，美国与沙特的协议已获得特朗普批准。 该报称，如果美国反对联合研究后在沙特阿拉伯进行铀浓缩活动，那么该王国在十年内将不得单独或与其他外国合作伙伴进行此类活动。 该计划现将提交给美国国会。预计政治两派的一些议员也将反对这项协议，尽管特朗普的共和党控制着上层和下层……

title.en: 'Exact opposite symbolism': Hitler's birthplace transformed to deter extremists
title.zh: “完全相反的象征意义”：希特勒出生地被改造以阻止极端分子

summary.en: Officials in an Austrian town have remodeled the building where Adolf Hitler was born. The transformation aims to prevent any association with him and deter extremist gatherings.
summary.zh: 奥地利一个城镇的官员对阿道夫·希特勒的出生地进行了改造。此次改造旨在避免与他产生任何关联，并阻止极端分子聚集。

body.en:
The building where Adolf Hitler was born, near the Austrian border with Germany, officially began a new life as a police station, a conversion Austria's government hopes will prevent it serving as a place of pilgrimage for neo-Nazis and far-right extremists.

After years of debate about the large terraced house in the town of Braunau am Inn, which was in private ownership and had housed a charity for people with disabilities, Austria made a compulsory purchase in 2017 and announced in 2019 it would be remodelled and turned into a police station.

Even before the conversion, the only sign of its historical significance was a rock on the pavement from the Mauthausen concentration camp with the inscription: "For Peace, Freedom and Democracy. Never Again Fascism. Millions of Dead Warn." It does not mention Hitler.

The rock remains in place. The only sign added to the white facade reads "Police".

"The aim was to prevent any association with Adolf Hitler, so as to strip it of that mystique", the head of the Austrian interior ministry's history department, Stephan Mlczoch, told reporters on a tour of the building.

That mystique was encouraged by the Nazis' cult of personality around Hitler, under whose rule the "Fuehrer birth house" was an art museum.

Hitler only lived there for a few weeks in 1889 before his family moved out, Mlczoch said.

The roughcast yellow walls of the home have been whitewashed over by the Austrian architecture firm Marte.

"Today's police, our Austrian federal police, is the exact opposite of the symbolism tied to this place. Our police stand ... for democracy and the rule of law," Interior Minister Gerhard Karner told an opening ceremony.

Passers-by often stop to take pictures, but their views on Hitler are usually not known. Local officials said there are now only "isolated incidents" involving visitors, fewer than before.

While they did not elaborate, the Hitler salute and other Nazi symbols are banned in Austria.

Asked about the public response to the project, local mayor Johannes Waidbacher told Reuters: "I think on the whole, the people of Braunau have accepted it and can live with it."

Waidbacher was on a commission that recommended the building be used either for a charitable or official administrative purpose.

In the end, having a charity based there would have made it too accessible to the public, he said.

"I think it isn't a bad approach but whether it works as we all hope and expect, we'll have to wait and see," he said.

title.en: House Republicans to write $95bn bill to fund Iran war and aid farmers
title.zh: 众议院共和党人将起草950亿美元法案，用于资助伊朗战争和援助农民

summary.en: House Republicans have agreed to draft a $95 billion bill to fund military operations in Iran and provide aid to farmers. The legislative move also includes an attempt to introduce new voting restrictions.
summary.zh: 众议院共和党人已同意起草一项950亿美元的法案，用于资助对伊朗的军事行动并向农民提供援助。这项立法举措还包括一项引入新投票限制的尝试。

body.en: GOP-controlled chamber paves way for reconciliation bill, while making long-shot attempt at new voting restrictions House Republicans on Wednesday agreed to begin the process of writing a $95bn bill to fund the war with Iran as well as provide new aid to farmers, while making a long-shot attempt to impose new restrictions on voting nationwide. In a virtually party-line 216-214, the Republican-controlled chamber passed a budget resolution that paves the way for the creation of a reconciliation bill, which can advance through the Senate under special rules that circumvent the Democratic filibuster and requires only a simple majority to pass. Two Republicans – Warren Davidson of Ohio and Thomas Massie of Kentucky, as well as Kevin Kiley, an independent of California – joined all Democrats in opposing the measure. Continue reading...
body.zh: 共和党控制的众议院为和解法案铺平道路，同时对新的投票限制进行了一次不太可能的尝试 众议院共和党人周三同意开始起草一项 950 亿美元的法案，为与伊朗的战争提供资金，并向农民提供新的援助，同时对全国投票实施新的限制进行一次不太可能的尝试。共和党控制的众议院几乎以216-214的党派路线通过了一项预算决议，为制定和解法案铺平了道路，该法案可以根据绕过民主党阻挠的特殊规则在参议院获得通过，并且只需要简单多数即可通过。两名共和党人——俄亥俄州的沃伦·戴维森(Warren Davidson)和肯塔基州的托马斯·马西(Thomas Massie)，以及加利福尼亚州的无党派人士凯文·基利(Kevin Kiley)——与所有民主党人一起反对这项措施。继续阅读...

title.en: California toddler bitten by rattlesnake ‘hiding under’ Amazon package

body.en: Three-year-old girl landed in ICU after snake bit her while grabbing a package outside her family’s Santa Clarita home A three-year-old girl landed in the intensive care unit earlier this month after a rattlesnake bit her while she was trying to grab an Amazon package. Addy, the young girl, ran out with her mother on 13 July to pick up a package dropped over the gate to their home in Santa Clarita, north of Los Angeles. Continue reading...

title.en: Fire kills 10 members of same family in Peru, police say
title.zh: 秘鲁警方称火灾导致同一家庭10名成员死亡

summary.en: Authorities are investigating the cause of the blaze in Lima as local media report it may have been arson.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A fire has killed 10 members of the same family, including five children, at a home in Peru's capital Lima, police say.

The blaze ripped through the property in the southern La Victoria district early on Wednesday, Gen Oscar Arriola from the Peruvian National Police told local media.

Five children, aged between three and 15 years old, were killed, as well as four adults aged between 29 and 72, and a fifth whose age was not given. Two people were also reportedly injured.

Police are investigating reports that the fire was started by arsonists. Local media say the family, who manufactured mattresses and owned electric motorcycles, had received threats and demands for extortion payments.

According to a report by the government news agency Andina , external , neighbours said unknown individuals had set fire to motorcycles parked outside, with the flames spreading rapidly through flammable mattress-making materials.

Seventeen members of the family were in the building when the fire started at 03:00 local time (08:00 GMT) but seven managed to escape, the Infobae news site , external reports.

Listing the exact ages of the victims, the police said the children were aged three, six, six, eight and 15. The adults were aged 29, 35, 42 and 72.

"Today, all of Peru falls silent in the face of a tragedy that plunges our nation into mourning," a statement from the National Police of Peru said.
body.zh: 警方称，秘鲁首都利马的一处住宅发生火灾，导致同一家庭的 10 名成员死亡，其中包括 5 名儿童。 秘鲁国家警察局局长奥斯卡·阿里奥拉 (Oscar Arriola) 告诉当地媒体，周三早些时候，大火席卷了南部拉维多利亚区的一处房产。 5 名年龄在 3 岁到 15 岁之间的儿童以及 4 名年龄在 29 岁到 72 岁之间的成年人被杀，还有 1 名年龄不详的人被杀。据报道还有两人受伤。 警方正在调查有关纵火犯纵火的报道。当地媒体称，这个生产床垫并拥有电动摩托车的家庭曾收到威胁和勒索付款要求。 据政府通讯社安迪纳对外报道，邻居称，不明身份的人放火焚烧了停在外面的摩托车，火焰通过易燃床垫制造材料迅速蔓延。 据 Infobae 新闻网站外部报道，当地时间 03:00（格林威治标准时间 08:00）起火时，该建筑内有 17 名家庭成员，但其中 7 人成功逃脱。 警方列出了受害者的具体年龄，称儿童年龄分别为三岁、六岁、六岁、八岁和 15 岁。成年人年龄分别为 29 岁、35 岁、42 岁和 72 岁。 秘鲁国家警察在一份声明中表示：“今天，面对这场让我们国家陷入哀悼的悲剧，整个秘鲁都保持沉默。”

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Police formally investigate woman after Brit stabbed to death in French village
title.zh: 法国警方正式调查一名女子涉嫌2025年英国公民遇害案

summary.en: French police have formally opened an investigation into the 2025 killing of Briton Karen Carter, who was found with stab wounds in the Dordogne village where she had resided for over a decade.
summary.zh: 法国警方已正式对2025年英国公民卡伦·卡特遇害案展开调查。卡特在法国多尔多涅省居住了十多年的村庄里被发现身中刀伤。

body.en:
A woman has been placed under formal investigation over the death last year in France of a British-South African mother-of-four.

Karen Carter, 65, was found lying near her car with stab wounds by a friend in Trémolat, the Dordogne village where she had lived for over a decade and managed two holiday rental homes.

Prosecutors say the 70-year-old woman was originally taken into custody in 2025 as part of preliminary inquiries before being released.

Jacques-Edouard Andrault, the investigating judge in the case, said in a statement on Wednesday that "the investigations conducted as part of the judicial inquiry opened on 7 May, 2025, have led the investigating judge to formally charge her".

Being placed under formal investigation in French law means an investigating judge has to decide whether or not there is enough evidence for the case to go to trial.

At the time of the killing in April last year, Karen Carter's husband, Alan, said that he first heard of her death through a cousin who had read about it on a local community Facebook page.

He said he received confirmation of the death after his assistant phoned local police.

Describing his wife as an outgoing, friendly person who "wouldn't hurt a fly", he said her death has been "traumatic" for his family.

"I'm an introvert, and she's the exact opposite. She's an extrovert, she loves people, she loves to have fun. People love her, she has a good heart," he said.

"She's the one who would bring home the lost dog, or cat, or whatever. She's that sort of person. Everyone liked her. That's why I married her. She's just lovely."
body.zh: 去年，一名英国裔南非四个孩子的母亲在法国死亡，一名妇女因此受到正式调查。 65 岁的凯伦·卡特 (Karen Carter) 在多尔多涅省特雷莫拉特 (Trémolat) 的一位朋友被发现躺在她的车旁，身上有刀伤。她在多尔多涅省特雷莫拉特 (Trémolat) 村生活了十多年，管理着两栋度假出租屋。 检察官表示，这名 70 岁的妇女最初于 2025 年被拘留，作为初步调查的一部分，随后被释放。 该案的预审法官雅克-爱德华·安德罗 (Jacques-Edouard Andrault) 在周三的一份声明中表示，“作为 2025 年 5 月 7 日启动的司法调查的一部分进行的调查，导致预审法官正式对她提出指控”。 2025 年 4 月凶杀案发生时，卡特夫人的丈夫艾伦 (Alan) 表示，他第一次听说卡特夫人的死讯是在一位表弟在当地社区 Facebook 页面上读到这起死亡事件后联系他时。 他说，在他的助手给当地警方打电话后，他收到了死亡确认。 他形容他的妻子是一个性格外向、友善的人，“不会伤害一只苍蝇”，他说她的死对他的家人来说是“创伤”。 “我是一个内向的人，而她恰恰相反。她是一个外向的人，她爱人，她喜欢玩得开心。人们爱她，她有一颗善良的心，”他说。 “她会把丢失的狗、猫或其他东西带回家。她就是这样的人。每个人都喜欢她。这就是我娶她的原因。她很可爱。”

reflection.en: The formal investigation into Karen Carter's death highlights the solemn duty to seek truth and justice for those who can no longer speak for themselves. In such tragic circumstances, the pursuit of accountability becomes a way to uphold the dignity of every life.
reflection.zh: 对卡伦·卡特死亡事件的正式调查，凸显了为那些无法为自己发声的人寻求真相和正义的庄严责任。在这样的悲剧中，追究责任成为维护每个生命尊严的一种方式。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Trump threatens to target Iran's bridges and power plants if Hormuz attacks persist
title.zh: 特朗普威胁称，如果霍尔木兹海峡袭击持续，将袭击伊朗的桥梁和发电厂

summary.en: Donald Trump says the US will respond any time Iranian forces shoot at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
President Donald Trump has threatened that the US would destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant any time its forces attack a ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

Potential targets would include ones "located next to, or in," the capital Tehran, he said in a post on Truth Social.

The military response would follow any form of attack on shipping in the vital waterway, "whether it be by missile, rocket, drone, or any other device or weapon".

His threat follows the US launching strikes on Iran for the 11th consecutive night, with Tehran warning the US against targeting its nuclear facilities.

Iranian state media reported that air defences were activated in the capital Tehran. Explosions were also reported in the north-western city of Tabriz, the south-eastern ports of Chabahar and Konarak, and in the southern city of Bushehr, home to Iran's only nuclear power plant.

Iran, which has retaliated against the US and its Middle East allies, warned of reprisals after Trump said the US would soon hit an underground nuclear site near Natanz.

Kuwait's army said on Wednesday that its air defences had engaged with drone attacks from Iran, while Bahrain and Jordan said they had also intercepted drone and missile strikes.

The price of oil jumped in response to the latest escalation, reaching $94 on Wednesday.

Iran's top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, warned the US on Wednesday evening that "the equation of this war is clear: either all or none!

"In a region where we do not sell oil, no-one will sell oil. If our security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe, and the security of the strait is in the absence of American forces. We have repeatedly said that the situation of the strait will not return to pre-war conditions," Ghalibaf wrote in a post on X.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier said Washington was still willing to engage in diplomacy with Tehran, but added that he did not believe Iran was serious about talks.

Prior to that, the US president said the next military target could be a complex known as Pickaxe Mountain , an underground nuclear site where Iran is suspected of building an undeclared enrichment facility.

Trump also threatened to "take care of" the Houthi rebels if the Iran-backed militant group in Yemen followed through on its threatened blockade of Saudi ports.

A Houthi media official had earlier said they were closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait - the Red Sea's southern gateway - to Saudi vessels.

The Red Sea has become crucial for oil shipments from Saudi Arabia during the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Following the Houthi announcement, two tankers which had just loaded Saudi crude bound for China and India at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port of Yanbu made U-turns...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统威胁称，只要美国军队袭击霍尔木兹海峡的一艘船只，美国就会摧毁伊朗的一座桥梁或发电厂。 他在 Truth Social 上发表的一篇文章中表示，潜在的目标将包括“位于首都德黑兰附近或境内”的目标。 军事反应将在对重要水道上的航运进行任何形式的攻击后做出，“无论是通过导弹、火箭、无人机还是任何其他装置或武器”。 在他发出威胁之前，美国已连续 11 晚对伊朗发动袭击，德黑兰警告美国不要针对其核设施。 伊朗官方媒体报道称，首都德黑兰启动了防空系统。据报道，西北部城市大不里士、东南部港口恰巴哈尔和科纳拉克以及伊朗唯一核电站所在地的南部城市布什尔也发生爆炸。 在特朗普表示美国将很快袭击纳坦兹附近的地下核设施后，对美国及其中东盟友进行报复的伊朗警告称，将采取报复行动。 科威特军队周三表示，其防空系统已应对来自伊朗的无人机袭击，而巴林和约旦表示，他们也拦截了无人机和导弹袭击。 由于最新的升级，油价跳涨，周三达到 94 美元。 伊朗最高谈判代表穆罕默德·巴格尔·加利巴夫周三晚间警告美国，“这场战争的等式很明确：要么全部，要么全无！ “在我们不出售石油的地区，没有人会出售石油。如果我们的安全得不到保证，基础设施就不会安全，海峡的安全就没有美军的存在。我们一再表示，海峡局势不会回到战前状态。”加利巴夫在X上发帖写道。 美国国务卿卢比奥早些时候表示，华盛顿仍然愿意与德黑兰进行外交，但他补充说，他不认为伊朗认真对待谈判。 此前，美国总统表示，下一个军事目标可能是一个名为镐山的综合体，这是一个地下核设施，伊朗怀疑在那里建造了一个未申报的浓缩设施。 特朗普还威胁说，如果伊朗支持的也门激进组织胡塞武装兑现其对沙特港口的封锁威胁，他将“照顾”胡塞叛军。 胡塞武装媒体官员早些时候表示，他们正在对沙特船只关闭红海南部门户曼德海峡。 在美以与伊朗的战争期间，红海对于沙特阿拉伯的石油运输至关重要，导致霍尔木兹海峡实际上被关闭。 胡塞武装宣布消息后，两艘刚刚在沙特阿拉伯红海延布港装载沙特原油前往中国和印度的油轮掉头……

title.en: Hungary: Ex-PM Orban pledges resistance to Magyar 'tyranny'
title.zh: 匈牙利：前总理欧尔班承诺抵制马扎尔“暴政”

summary.en: Hungary's former prime minister alleges that his successor has "dismantled the rule of law and eliminated checks and balances." Peter Magyar has pursued Viktor Orban and his allies since winning April's elections.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 匈牙利前总理声称他的继任者“破坏了法治并取消了制衡”。自赢得四月选举以来，彼得·马扎尔（Peter Magyar）一直在追捕维克托·欧尔班（Viktor Orban）及其盟友。 匈牙利前总理维克托·欧尔班周三指责检察官和新政府对其青民盟进行虚假调查，一天前，调查人员在腐败调查中从布达佩斯青民盟总部没收了设备。 匈牙利长期领导人欧尔班在四月份的大选中以压倒性优势输给了保守派竞争对手彼得·马扎尔（Peter Magyar），他本人也是青民盟前成员，这一结果受到欧洲大部分地区的欢迎，但特朗普政府却不这么认为。 自上台以来，马扎尔已着手消除他所称的欧尔班和青民盟时代的系统性腐败，并做出了一系列彻底的改变。然而，欧尔班周三称这些措施是“暴政”的迹象，并表示他和他的反对党将通过一切和平手段进行“抵抗”。 欧尔班周二晚间在网上发表的声明，以及周三在青民盟总部外举行的新闻发布会，构成了他执政 16 年后于 5 月初重返反对派领导人以来的两次最强烈的政治声明。 在他的政党宣布检察官搜查了该党总部并没收了计算机服务器和其他材料后不久，他就在脸书上首次发表了所谓的“抵抗声明”。这是对该国国家文化基金腐败调查的一部分，该基金据称是欧尔班核心圈子的国营支付中心和影子选举竞选基金。 欧尔班声称，“国家文化基金问题只是这次[搜查党总部]的借口”，他否认有任何不当行为。 他说，在新的中右翼政府利用其议会绝对多数通过宪法修正案，终止总统和宪法法院院长的授权后，匈牙利“不再是一个民主国家”——两人都被视为欧尔班的盟友。他表示，他和他的政党将“采用一切和平手段”反对“非法”的政治制度。 周三，在青民盟行动基地外，欧尔班表示，他相信马扎尔试图一劳永逸地阻碍他的政党。 “到昨天，我才意识到这一切是怎么回事，”他告诉记者。 “事实是，这成为了夺取青民盟服务器的借口……这是一项出于政治动机的法律程序，旨在使青民盟——显然在这场严重的政治失败中幸存下来并且正在变得更加强大——在法律上变得不可行。” 彼得·马扎尔 (Peter Magyar) 的新政党蒂萨 (Tisza) 轻松获胜......

A modelling scout linked to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein has been found dead at his home.

Daniel Siad, 69, was discovered on Monday in Colombes, a north-west suburb of Paris, the Nanterre prosecutor's office confirmed.

An investigation to determine the cause of death was opened on Monday evening, the office said, adding that a post-mortem examination would be carried out.

Siad's name appeared thousands of times in the Epstein files released by the US government. He denied knowing of the threat Epstein had posed.

The Paris prosecutor's office has defended an investigation it launched in February, saying there had been insufficient evidence to justify arresting Siad.

"The investigation opened on 18 February 2026 covering charges of organised human trafficking and conspiracy to commit a crime is continuing in order to identify all individuals potentially involved despite the termination of criminal proceedings against Daniel Siad," the office said.

"Daniel Siad was subject to special investigative techniques, notably telephone surveillance, but they did not provide enough evidence justifying his immediate arrest," it added.

Siad had been the subject of several complaints in France including allegations of rape.

The dead man's lawyer stressed that Siad had "never been prosecuted". "He is dead and he was innocent," Ménya Arab-Tigrine said in a statement.

Epstein victim Anya - not her real name - previously told the BBC that Siad had introduced her to Epstein .

"It was a complete set-up," she said, describing Siad as "essentially a professional trafficker".

During one email to Epstein released in the files, Siad wrote in badly spelled English: "In This busyness I feel like fisherman some time I cache quick, some time no fish."

Ahead of a BBC investigation on the subject published on Saturday, Arab-Tigrine had said her client was not available for comment.

However, in a recent CNN interview, Siad said he had not known the women were being abused by Epstein. "I trusted him, I believed this guy is a professional person," he said.

The first complaints against Siad in France were filed in February. He denied wrongdoing in multiple recent media interviews, telling BFMTV in May: "I have never raped anyone in my life."

Lawyers for the former model who made the first complaint said earlier that they were "stunned" by his death.

"We are at a loss for words to describe the anger and sadness we feel," they said, with alleged victims "denied a criminal trial".

title.en: Who could be the next UN Secretary-General?
title.zh: 谁将成为下一任联合国秘书长？

summary.en: For the first time in a decade, the United Nations is preparing to select its next Secretary-General. The report examines six candidates, their platforms, and the significant challenges awaiting them and the global organization.
summary.zh: 联合国将十年来首次选出新任秘书长。报道审视了六位候选人，他们的主张，以及他们和联合国将面临的重大挑战。

body.en:
For the first time in a decade, the United Nations will soon choose a new Secretary-General. DW takes a look at the six candidates, what they stand for and the challenges they and the UN will face.

After a decade in power, Antonio Guterres , will end his second term as UN Secretary-General on December 31. There are currently six candidates lining up to replace him. Whoever emerges victorious has a tough task, with the relevance, power and financial capability of the UN under an increasingly harsh spotlight.

The UN Secretary-General is "equal parts diplomat and advocate, civil servant and CEO,"  according to the organization itself. The holder of the position oversees several vital UN organs, including the Security Council , charged with maintaining peace and security.

The winning candidate will be selected by the UN's General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council (whose permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States), making the path to victory narrow and fraught.

Here's what you need to know about each candidate ahead of a debate between them on Thursday (July 23) at the UN's General Assembly Hall in New York.

The first female president of Chile (from 2006 to 2010 and then 2014 to 2018) is vying to become the first female UN Secretary-General, after several women lost out to Guterres in 2016. "If I am polite, I would say the world was not prepared for it. Is it prepared now? I hope so," Bachelet, 74, said earlier this year. "It will be a very good signal," she said, adding that it would provide hope for many people.

Bachelet also served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights between 2018 and 2022, a position which saw her involved in many of the key geopolitical issues she would face if elected.  While she has admitted she has no "magic formula" to resolve the issues on the Security Council, Bachelet has sought to talk up her experience as a key asset.

The Argentine diplomat has spent most of his career in the nuclear and atomic energy sectors, culminating in his 2019 appointment as director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) , an autonomous organization within the UN.

Given the geopolitical landscape, with nuclear war perceived as an increasing threat , Grossi sees his background as "clearly an advantage. You have to understand the world you live in," he told Swiss outlet Geneva Solutions.

Grossi supports the UN's current attempt at reform known as UN80 and says there is "no need to reinvent the wheel" but wants to streamline the organization with mergers of UN entities and reductions in "duplications, triplications, even quadruplications or quintuplications of structures," which add significant costs to members.

title.en: How Russia is luring foreign nationals to fight in Ukraine
title.zh: 俄罗斯如何引诱外国人到乌克兰参战

summary.en: More and more, Russia is recruiting men from the world’s poorest countries to send them to the front in the Ukraine war. Why are people joining up?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
More and more, Russia is recruiting men from the world’s poorest countries to send them to the front in the Ukraine war. Why are people joining up?

Charles Mutoka, a 72-year-old  Kenyan is in mourning for his son, Oscar Khagola Mutoka, a former soldier who traveled to Russia  in the summer of 2025 to look for work.

His father said that he had tried in vain to talk him out of it. Oscar did not tell him and the rest of his family exactly where he was going but a week after leaving he sent a picture of himself in uniform and never got back in touch again.

His family found out that he had died some time later but, despite appeals to the Kenyan authorities, they were not able to recover the body. 

In May 2026, the family held a symbolic memorial service and set up a makeshift burial site for Oscar, in order to at least have a place where they could pray. "The worst part is that I don't know if and where he was actually buried, or if his body was simply dumped in a forest in Russia," Charles Mutoka said.

Oscar Mutoka is one of an estimated 27,000 or more foreign nationals recruited by Russia for its war in Ukraine, according to the Defense Intelligence of Ukraine  (HUR). A joint study conducted by the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), the Truth Houndshuman rights organization and the Kazakhstan International Bureau for Human Rights and Rule of Law (KIBHR) provides evidence that Russia has set up a global network for recruiting foreign nationals.

"This recruitment targets people in economically, socially and legally precarious life situations. The methods employed range from enticing offers to deception and even coercion," Ilya Nusov, one of the authors of the study, told DW.

For many people living in the world's poorest regions, the wages offered by the Russian army is a huge incentive as it means a chance to escape poverty and support their families. That's exactly why Yoan Viondi Mendoza, a Cuban national, decided to work in Russia. He was promised $2,000 (€1,750) per month, an enormous sum by Cuban standards, where the average wage is $20 (€17,50). 

DW found out about Yoan Mendoza's story from his brother Michael Duro, who lives in the US . Yoan had wanted to emigrate to the US and be reunited with his brother, but this turned out to be impossible, because of financial and bureaucratic hurdles.

Then he came across a job offer in Russia, his brother said. "Yoan called and said he'd found a way out. He told me about a 'project' in Russia," said Duro, who told DW that he had tried in vain to change his brother's mind.

title.en: Germany's growing interest in Africa: A win for both sides?
title.zh: 德国对非洲日益增长的兴趣：对双方都是双赢吗？

summary.en: Germany is increasing its engagement with African nations, with Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul undertaking his third visit to the continent in 2026. Discussions during these high-level talks are centered on security cooperation, skills development, and investment opportunities.
summary.zh: 德国正深化其在非洲的影响力，外交部长约翰·瓦德普尔将于2026年第三次访问非洲大陆。他的高级别会谈将聚焦于安全、技能发展和投资。

body.en:
Germany is deepening its footprint across Africa, as Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul embarks on his third trip to the continent in 2026. His top-level talks will focus on security, skills development and investment.

Wadephul is currently visiting Nigeria as part of a multi-country trip across Africa, after a major stopover in Mauritania, and before making a call on South Africa.

The trip follows up on prior journeys to Africa by Germany's top diplomat, who visited Ethiopia and Kenya in January, and Morocco in April.

Wadephul says these repeated travels to the continent are a strategic necessity as part of Germany's expanding engagement with Africa.

"This is my third trip to Africa now. Why? Africa is a continent of both destiny and opportunity for Europe," he told reporters, highlighting the continent's economic potential while also pointing out persistent security challenges.

Wadephul's stop in Mauritania focused on various interlinked issues such as security cooperation, migration management and regional stability.

Geopolitical analyst Fidel Amakye Owusu said that Germany was interested in "Mauritania because of migration," highlighting the growing use of Atlantic migration routes by people desperate to reach Europe.

The German foreign minister's visit came just days after the UN refugee agency reported at least 144 deaths along this route near the Mauritanian coast.

Wadephul's visit, however, also focused on opportunities for deeper security cooperation with Mauritania; his delegation visited the Mourchidates, an all-female Islamic spiritual guide group trained and deployed by the state to counter extremism.

DW's Silja Fröhlich, who accompanied Wadephul on the trip, noted that the foreign minister's interaction with the Mourchidates was one of the main highlights: "In Mauritania, he was visibly moved by women working with the UN to prevent extremism and violence — women who, despite living in a deeply patriarchal society and often carrying personal ties to the very conflict they are confronting, are determined to protect their communities," she explained.

Support for such a grassroots initiative is also a reflection of Germany's intent on bolstering community‑based approaches to preventing radicalization.

As part of the second leg in  Nigeria , Wadephul has met with various entrepreneurs, creatives, influencers, filmmakers and students.

"We are looking for new global partners. This is the very reason that I am here: that we are looking to Africa and to the countries in Africa. title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test
title.zh: “强烈关切”：澳大利亚在中国弹道导弹试验后与中方会晤

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

title.en: 'Business-friendly socialism': What are new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's policies?
title.zh: “商业友好型社会主义”：英国新首相安迪·伯纳姆的政策是什么？

summary.en: The United Kingdom's new prime minister, Andy Burnham, has outlined his policy agenda, which includes measures such as energy cuts, rent controls, and approaches to Brexit.

body.en:
Andy Burnham, sworn in this week as the United Kingdom's seventh prime minister in a decade, has opened his tenure with a slew of new policies, branding his own political ideology as "business-friendly socialism".

Burnham was sworn in as the UK's new prime minister on Monday, replacing Keir Starmer, who resigned following months of pressure from his own MPs after just over two years in the job.

The former Greater Manchester mayor, nicknamed the 'King of the North' for his defence of the region during his nine-year stint as mayor, used his first days in office to signal a new leftward shift for the Labour government.

On his first full day, Burnham told the inaugural meeting of his cabinet that he would lead a "cost of living government".

Burnham has branded his political ideology "business-friendly socialism" — with a distinct focus on cost of living measures.

He has unveiled some early policies designed "to do some things that people will feel and feel quite quickly", especially those on the lowest incomes — adding that a longer-term plan would be set out later in the year.

On Tuesday, Burnham announced he will cut taxes on electricity bills — one of the main drivers of the UK's cost of living crisis — in his first move to ease pressures that have angered the public and helped stoke political instability.

Burnham said his government would remove the value-added tax from domestic electricity bills from 1 October, cutting about £45 ($86) from the average annual bill of about £1,860 ($3,554) that households pay.

"We're taking immediate action to cut taxes on energy bills, put more money in people's pockets and bring back hope," Burnham said in a statement, having pledged to give people more "breathing space" in their lives.

The government said it would be funded by cancelling Starmer's plan for a digital ID scheme that would have cost the taxpayer £1.8 billion ($3.44 billion) — but former minister Darren Jones said the ID program had been "unfunded".

The energy announcement is designed to show that Burnham will move quickly to improve living standards after years of stagnation.

He said on Monday his early policies might not "take all of the pressure off" people struggling with rising prices, and that his 10-year plan will be unveiled later this year.

During his first speech as prime minister on Monday, Burnham also said his first ambition was to end rough sleeping in the UK.

He is reportedly considering rent control measures, alongside plans to build more public housing to help bring down welfare spending.

title.en: Flights to return after 40-year hiatus as Trump promises to help Lebanon 'a lot'
title.zh: 航班在中断40年后恢复，特朗普承诺“大力”帮助黎巴嫩

summary.en: Flights between Lebanon and Israel are set to resume after a 40-year suspension. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated his objective is a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump vowed on Wednesday to help Lebanon "a lot" as its president, Joseph Aoun, sought the US' backing for a fragile effort to disarm Hezbollah and forge a path to peace with Israel.

Meeting Aoun at the White House, Trump said Lebanon had been "a very mistreated country" that had been "hit hard" for decades.

"It's probably a dangerous place in a lot of ways," Trump told reporters. "But they love the country ... and we're going to help it. We're going to help it a lot."

Aoun, the first Lebanese president invited to Washington since 2009, asked Trump for political support and continued backing for the Lebanese army, which has begun deploying in southern areas under a US-backed framework agreement with Israel.

"We need to support the LAF," Aoun said, referring to the Lebanese Armed Forces. "Without the LAF, everything will collapse."

Aoun's nearly two-hour visit took place as Israeli troops continue to occupy a swath of the country's south and hundreds of thousands of Lebanese remain displaced following Israeli strikes. Hezbollah has rejected the government's direct talks with Israel as well as efforts by the state to disarm it.

The talks highlighted Aoun's delicate balancing act — seeking Trump's help to secure an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon while simultaneously facing pressure from the US and Israel to disarm Hezbollah, which remains a formidable fighting force despite recent setbacks.

The Lebanese president, a former army commander, said the military was "the backbone of security and stability" and the country's most trusted institution.

In a statement after the talks, the Lebanese presidency said Aoun stressed to Trump the "urgent need for a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory," calling it "an essential step to consolidate stability and enable the Lebanese state to extend its full sovereignty exclusively through its own forces."

Following his meeting with Aoun, Trump said he would direct his administration to allow all US airline carriers to fly directly to Lebanon— a historic policy shift more than 40 years in the making.

US flights were suspended in 1985 after the hijacking of TWA Flight 847 from Athens, Greece, en route to Rome, Italy, that was forced to land in Beirut. During the 17-day ordeal, a US Navy diver was brutally killed.

The Federal Aviation Administration and Transportation Department did not immediately comment.

Trump's visit came as the Lebanese army moved into an area of the south under a deal with Israel aimed at proving Lebanon can extend state authority and disarm Iran-backed Hezbollah.

body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. But workers’ writing has seen a revival in the 21st century. This time, it is bottom-up rather than directed from above. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? summary.en: Isabel Rose was convicted of trying to extort £100,000 from the UK banker and perverting the course of justice.

body.en:
A British woman has been jailed for six years in Hong Kong for blackmail and perverting the course of justice after a court found she made a false allegation of rape.

Isabel Rose, 26, from Hackney in east London, alleged that a British banker raped her after she travelled to Hong Kong to visit him in January 2024.

The man was arrested after she reported the incident but later released without charge. Rose was subsequently arrested and charged.

Local media reported that Rose was in Hong Kong's District Court on Wednesday for sentencing after being convicted in March. She had denied the charges.

According to local press reports, Judge Adriana Tse sentenced her to five years in prison for blackmail and three years for perverting the course of justice, with one year to be served consecutively.

Prosecutors argued that Rose fabricated the allegation in an attempt to extort £100,000 ($134,000) from the man, whose identity was withheld. Rose denied the charges throughout the trial and has consistently maintained that she was raped.

Rose had travelled to Hong Kong on 31 January 2024 after meeting the man while in Thailand a month earlier, according to court documents.

At the centre of the prosecution case were WhatsApp messages exchanged between the pair in the hours and days after the alleged rape on 1 February at his apartment.

In one message sent the following morning, Rose wrote: "Are you annoyed I didn't want to have sex," to which the man replied: "What no of course not. Was impressed by your restraint."

Later that day, Rose wrote: "You violated me last night, I didn't wanna have sex."

He replied: "I'm really deeply sorry, I was slightly drunk and I misread your signals, it's no excuse and I know it doesn't make it any better."

In a later exchange, Rose wrote: "You basically raped me." The man replied: "That's not what I'm into at all and I feel sick."

The pair later exchanged messages about money. According to the written judgement of the verdict published in March, the man agreed to reimburse Rose for her travel and accommodation.

In one message, Rose wrote: "Send me the right amount you owe me for everything. Think about that. Think carefully."

Rose subsequently wrote: "You've given 10% of what I'm owed. 100% of my soul gone."

In a later message, the man wrote: "But I don't have 100k, I have no way of paying you that."

Rose reported the rape to police on 3 February. The man was arrested and questioned before being released without charge. Rose was arrested the following day and later charged with blackmail and perverting the course of public justice.

In her verdict, Judge AN Tse Ching relied in part on the messages exchanged after the encounter, according to the South China Morning Post , external .

title.en: Can India become the next semiconductor hub after Taiwan?
title.zh: 印度能否成为继台湾之后的下一个半导体中心？

summary.en: India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.

More than 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductor chips are made in Taiwan , an island at the center of ongoing rivalry between the US and China .

Any disruption to Taiwan's chip industry would likely send shockwaves through the global economy, with modern semiconductors used to make everything from smartphones and electric vehicles (EVs) to aircraft and military systems .

During the COVID-19 pandemic, chip shortages forced automakers to halt production — exposing how dependent the world had become on a handful of manufacturers in East Asia.

The result has been a global race to build more resilient semiconductor supply chains. The US, Japan, South Korea and also the EU have all launched multi-billion-dollar programs to attract chipmakers.

India is now mounting its biggest push yet to become part of that network and enter the global arena as the next electronics powerhouse.

Last week, the Indian government approved a $13.2 billion (€11.4 billion) semiconductor program labeled Semicon 2.0. The project builds on the $9 billion India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched in 2021 and aims to develop the entire chip ecosystem — from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, specialty materials, equipment manufacturing and workforce training. 

Thousands of engineers working for companies such as Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments already design some of the world's most sophisticated chips from research centers in the Indian cities of Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Noida.

But analysts warn India has been lagging behind in large-scale manufacturing. In the semiconductor industry,  this is the area that brings both economic value and strategic importance.

"India already has the expertise to design sophisticated semiconductor chips," said V Kamakoti, director of the Indian Institute of Technology in the city of Madras.

"Indian engineers working for both domestic companies and multinational firms have successfully designed and delivered complex chips," Kamakoti told DW. "The bigger challenge is manufacturing them."

So far, India's progress has been concentrated in chip packaging and testing rather than manufacturing the chips themselves.

Kamakoti said the next step is building a domestic fabrication ecosystem that can turn those design strengths into large-scale production.

Micron Technology, a US memory chip maker, Kaynes Semicon and CG Semi, two Indian semiconductor assembly and packaging companies, have begun commercial production under the first phase of India's semiconductor program.

title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test
title.zh: “强烈关切”：澳大利亚在中国弹道导弹试验后与中方会晤

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

title.en: China narrows AI gap, challenges US influence
title.zh: 中国缩小人工智能差距，挑战美国影响力

summary.en: At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, China showcased its advancements in AI technology and promoted its vision for open-source development and global governance in the field, signaling a challenge to existing international influence.
summary.zh: 在上海举行的世界人工智能大会上，中国展示了其在人工智能技术方面的进展，并推广了其在开源开发和全球治理方面的愿景，这预示着对现有国际影响力的挑战。

body.en:
At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Beijing showcased advances in AI while promoting its vision of open-source development and global governance.

As China narrows the artificial intelligence (AI) gap with the United States,  Beijing is promoting a narrative centered on "open source" and "inclusive AI" as an argument for its vision of global governance.

During his keynote speech at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai on Friday, Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed China's ambition to take a leading role in setting global standards in AI . He criticized what he described as the "overextension of the concept of national security."

Xi did not openly reference the United States. However, Beijing's effort to position itself as an advocate of a new AI order and challenge US dominance was unmistakable.

This year's Shanghai summit sent several important signals, says Rogier Creemers, assistant professor at Leiden University in the Netherlands specializing in China's digital technology policy. The WAIC indicates that artificial intelligence is now one of Beijing's political priorities, and that China intends to compete with the United States by supporting open-source AI models and promoting AI-driven industrialization, Creemers told DW. He also noted China hopes to win support from countries in the Global South for this effort.

China is steadily narrowing the gap with the United States in AI model development, and its efforts at AI application in industrial processes are slowly maturing. 

Chinese AI model developers have continued to keep pace on the global stage, largely by training open-weight models on limited but advanced computer hardware, Paul Triolo, senior vice president for China and tech policy lead at DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group, told DW.

Triolo believes deployment of AI across Chinese enterprises may be progressing faster than in the United States.

In addition, there is less fear of AI among the Chinese population than there is in the US, facilitating more rapid uptake of AI applications at the consumer level.

Earlier this year, Chinese state media claimed that the performance gap between Chinese and US AI models had "largely disappeared."

Several experts broadly agreed with this assessment, saying that certain benchmark tests of China's  large language models (LLMs) such as GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3 showed the gap narrowing or even fully closing.

For most applications, Triolo noted, China's leading open-weight AI models are cheaper to run and more than capable of handling most tasks.

body.zh: 在上海举行的世界人工智能大会上，北京展示了人工智能的进步，同时宣传其开源发展和全球治理的愿景。 随着中国缩小与美国的人工智能 (AI) 差距，北京正在推动以“开源”和“包容性人工智能”为中心的叙事，作为其全球治理愿景的论据。 中国国家主席习近平周五在上海举行的世界人工智能大会（WAIC）上发表主旨演讲时表达了中国在制定人工智能全球标准方面发挥主导作用的雄心。他批评他所说的“国家安全概念的过度延伸”。 习近平没有公开提及美国。 然而，北京将自己定位为人工智能新秩序倡导者并挑战美国主导地位的努力是明确无误的。 荷兰莱顿大学专门研究中国数字技术政策的助理教授罗吉尔·克里默斯表示，今年的上海峰会发出了几个重要信号。 Creemers 告诉德国之声，WAIC 表明人工智能现在是北京的政治优先事项之一，中国打算通过支持开源人工智能模型和促进人工智能驱动的工业化来与美国竞争。他还指出，中国希望为此赢得南方国家的支持。 中国在人工智能模型开发方面与美国的差距正在稳步缩小，人工智能在工业流程中的应用也正在慢慢成熟。 DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group 中国区高级副总裁兼技术政策负责人 Paul Triolo 告诉德国之声，中国人工智能模型开发人员继续在全球舞台上保持同步，主要是在有限但先进的计算机硬件上训练开放权重模型。 Triolo 认为，中国企业的人工智能部署进展可能比美国更快。 此外，中国民众对人工智能的恐惧程度低于美国民众，这有助于消费者更快速地接受人工智能应用。 今年早些时候，中国官方媒体声称中国和美国人工智能模型之间的性能差距已经“基本消失”。 多位专家普遍同意这一评估，并表示，GLM-5.2和Kimi K3等中国大型语言模型（LLM）的某些基准测试表明，差距正在缩小甚至完全缩小。 Triolo 指出，对于大多数应用程序来说，中国领先的开放式人工智能模型的运行成本更低，并且能够处理大多数任务。 与此同时，Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Google 等美国领先公司的先进专有模型仍然在以下领域保持优势……

reflection.en: The rapid advancements in AI and visions for global technological governance highlight humanity's remarkable ingenuity and ambition. Yet, Yahweh's ancient warning from Genesis 11:6 reminds us to consider the spirit behind such endeavors, lest our pursuit of limitless capability overshadow the wisdom of humility and collaboration. reflection.zh: 人工智能的快速发展和全球技术治理的愿景，彰显了人类非凡的创造力和雄心。然而，雅伟在创世记11:6中的古老警示提醒我们，要审视这些努力背后的精神，以免我们对无限能力的追求，掩盖了谦逊和协作的智慧。真正的进步不仅在于我们能取得什么成就，更在于我们如何带着对终极依赖的认知来管理这些力量。

title.en: China, Philippines clash in South China Sea ahead of ASEAN meeting
title.zh: 东盟会议前夕，中国与菲律宾在南海发生冲突

summary.en: China and the Philippines traded accusations after a violent altercation between navy personnel in the disputed South China Sea. The incident heightened tensions ahead of a major diplomatic summit in Manila.
summary.zh: 在南海争议水域，中国和菲律宾海军人员发生暴力冲突后，两国相互指责。这一事件在马尼拉举行的一次重要外交峰会前夕加剧了紧张局势。

body.en:
China and the Philippines traded accusations after a violent altercation between navy personnel in the disputed South China Sea. The incident heightened tensions ahead of a major diplomatic summit in Manila.

Sailors from the Chinese and Philippine navies faced off with oars and batons in the disputed South China Sea , with Philippine officials saying that one of its sailors suffered a head injury as a result of the altercation.

The latest confrontation took place on Monday near the Second Thomas Shoal, a contested area where the two countries have  repeatedly clashed before . The  Philippines keeps a military presence in the area aboard the grounded warship BRP Sierra Madre.

Manila said that Chinese Coast Guard personnel had assaulted Filipino sailors as they approached the outpost. 

China quickly rejected this narrative. Beijing's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that the "Philippine side provoked the incident first," by approaching the Chinese vessel in small rubber boats, but then "turned around ​and made counter-accusations, distorted the facts and engaged in malicious ​hype."

On Tuesday, China summoned the Philippine ambassador in Beijing to lodge its complaints, with the Philippines quickly following suit with the Chinese counterpart in Manila.

The Second Thomas Shoal is part of the Spratly islands, a disputed archipelago in the South China Sea.

The Spratlys are key to Beijing's claim of the entire South China Sea, a key global trade route. Beijing maintains its claim to the waterway despite a 2016 ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague that there is no legal basis to its argument.

China has repeatedly demanded the removal of the outpost on the BRP Sierra Madre, and surrounded the atoll with its ships in a tense territorial standoff that has dragged on for years.

The incident came just ahead of a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) which was set to begin on Tuesday with foreign ministers of the eleven member states and external partners.

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong, who was in Manila for the summit, denounced Beijing on Tuesday for what she called "destabilizing and dangerous conduct" during the standoff.

Wong, during a visit to the headquarters of the Philippine Coast Guard, also announced a support package for the agency totaling 10 million Australian dollars ($6.7 million) for drone technology.

The US State Department also issued a statement criticizing China's actions, saying its "troubling pattern of provocations against the Philippines' legitimate maritime operations undermines regional peace and stability."

title.en: Chinese, Philippine personnel clash in the South China Sea
title.zh: 中菲人员在南海发生冲突

summary.en: Chinese Coast Guard and Philippine Navy personnel clashed in the South China Sea, resulting in a Philippine sailor sustaining a serious head injury. The incident involved the use of wooden batons during a confrontation between their boats.
summary.zh: 中国海警人员与菲律宾海军人员在南海发生冲突，双方船只上的队员使用木棍对峙，导致一名菲律宾水兵头部受重伤。

body.en: China Coast Guard personnel on a rigid hull inflatable boat clashed with Philippine Navy personnel aboard a rubber boat using wooden batons in the South China Sea on 20 July. According to Philippine authorities, one of their sailors suffered a serious head injury when a Chinese crew member allegedly struck him with a wooden baton.
body.zh: 7月20日，中国海警人员乘坐刚性充气艇与菲律宾海军人员乘坐橡皮艇在南海使用木棍发生冲突。据菲律宾当局称，一名中国船员据称用木棍殴打一名水手，导致其头部严重受伤。

reflection.en: The physical clash between personnel in the South China Sea highlights the fragility of peace in contested regions. Yahweh's word calls us to pursue peace actively, as far as it depends on us, even amidst disagreements. This incident reminds us of the constant need for restraint and diplomatic efforts to prevent escalation and injury.
reflection.zh: 南海人员之间的肢体冲突凸显了争议地区和平的脆弱性。雅伟的话语呼吁我们，只要力所能及，就要积极追求和平，即使在分歧之中也是如此。这一事件提醒我们，需要时刻保持克制并进行外交努力，以防止冲突升级和人员受伤。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections
title.zh: “令人震惊的漏洞”：特朗普就中国干预美国大选发表全面声明

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.
summary.zh: 美国总统就选举安全问题发表了广泛声明，为联邦政府采取行动奠定了基础。

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

"Over a period of years, starting during the 2020 election cycle, the People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history," Trump said in the televised speech from the White House.

He asserted that members of the US intelligence community deliberately suppressed information about the extent of China's activities.

His allegations contradict an unclassified 2021 US intelligence community assessment that found no indications any foreign actor tried to alter or succeeded in altering "any technical aspect" of the 2020 presidential election vote.

The assessment was conducted under John Ratcliffe, then Trump's director of national intelligence and now his CIA director.

Trump also claimed there were more than 250,000 non-US citizens registered to vote in four states.

Trump has persistently claimed his 2020 election defeat was "rigged," although more than 60 lawsuits produced no ruling establishing fraud capable of changing the outcome, while recounts, audits and his own justice department found none.

After railing against election security in the 25-minute address, Trump pressed Republicans in Congress to pass his signature elections legislation, the SAVE America Act, which has been stalled for months.

It seeks to impose new voter identification and citizenship requirements, despite longstanding findings that voter fraud in US elections is rare.

Election security experts have said these measures would make it harder for millions of eligible voters to cast a ballot.

title.en: The superannuation 'blind spot' funding Australian gambling companies

summary.en: Australians are losing more money per capita to gambling than any other country — about $32 billion a year.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia's 20 biggest superannuation funds have almost $15 billion invested in gambling-related companies, despite growing concern about the social harm caused by the industry.

A report released on Thursday by the Alliance for Gambling Reform found the sector holds $14.8 billion in gambling stocks.

Australia's largest fund, Australian Super, has the biggest exposure at $4.9 billion — more than double any other fund — while Australian Retirement Trust, Colonial First State, UniSuper and Aware Super round out the top five.

Gambling company Aristocrat Leisure is just one of the companies into which retirement funds are flowing.

Despite many funds having responsible investment policies, approaches to gambling-related risks remain "limited, inconsistent and largely inadequate", according to chief executive of the Alliance for Gambling Reform, Martin Thomas.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

He said many Australians would be shocked to learn how much of their money was being invested into the industry.

"There's starting to be a realisation just of how socially damaging gambling is," he told AAP.

Harms from gambling are not consistently treated the same way as harms arising from other industries such as tobacco and alcohol, he said, with the latter routinely screened out of superannuation investments.

Australians are losing more money per capita to gambling than any other country — about $32 billion a year.

A spokesperson for Australian Super said apart from its Socially Aware option, the fund does not apply investment screens to gambling companies.

"We invest to help members achieve their best financial position in retirement," they said.

"'We engage with certain ASX-listed companies either directly or with other investors to better understand their initiatives to deliver responsible gaming practices and appropriate governance practices."

Super funds could make more ethical choices about where they put their money, he said, noting gambling investment was a relatively small part of their overall investments, which may range in the hundreds of billions of dollars.

"There is so much opportunity out there for them to do the right thing," he said.

Thomas urged those who were concerned to contact their super fund to find out how much they were investing in gambling.

"We're not looking to ban gambling; we just think it's a harmful legal adult product and should be regulated," he said.

"But we do think it should be shunned by the investment community, particularly super funds, particularly because we're all made to contribute to these super funds."

title.en: Danni was diagnosed with bowel cancer at 39. It made her rethink what she ate growing up

body.en:

Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) comprise up to 50 per cent of our calories. And while some provide significant nutrients for a balanced diet, others could be responsible for damage in every major bodily organ. So, what are UPFs, and are they as bad as they're made out to be? Watch Insight episode Processed Food Fight on SBS On Demand.

At 39, after a period of feeling very fatigued and getting subsequent testing, Danni Duncan was diagnosed with stage 2 bowel cancer last year.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The Melbourne-based fitness coach then went down a rabbit hole researching contributing factors that can lead to bowel cancer and wondered if the ultra-processed foods (UPFs) she ate growing up could have contributed to the cause.

"Alongside other contributing factors — of course, it's not just the ultra-processed food — one of the common denominators was this big influx of ultra-processed food through the 90s."

While direct causality between UPFs and cancer has not been established, a study based at Massachusetts General Hospital led by Dr Andrew Chan found an association between high consumption of UPFs and an increased risk of having abnormal growths in the bowel, which can lead to cancer.

Danni says she ate a lot of UPFs growing up and that her childhood was "very highly ultra-processed".

"Breakfasts were Coco Pops, Rice Bubbles with sugar on top ... Tiny Teddies, Shapes, chips, Nutella, ham sandwiches on Wonder White bread and McDonald's."

'Ultra-processed' foods (such as confectionary and soft drinks) are products that have been industrially manufactured — containing ingredients such as preservatives and additives that would not be found in the home.

And Australians are among the leading consumers of UPFs, according to Phillip Baker, a public health researcher at The University of Sydney.

"We're eating somewhere between 40 and 50 percent of our calories from ultra-processed foods," Baker said.

Unlike 'processed' foods, UPFs have only been part of our diet for the past 70-80 years.

Processed foods are altered from their natural state — often with simple ingredients such as salt, oil or sugar — for safety, convenience and shelf life; while UPFs often have five ingredients or more and contain additives and little wholefood.

body.en:
Census night is Tuesday 11 August, and every person in Australia — including Norfolk Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Christmas Island — must be counted.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) conducts a Census of Population and Housing every five years to gather what officials describe as a snapshot of the nation.

It includes up to 66 questions spanning a person's ancestry, religious affiliation, sex recorded at birth and even how they commuted to work that day.

Emily Walter, a Census national spokesperson at the ABS, said many people will be completing the Census for the first time.

"There's a lot of Australians who won't have done a Census before, and this is really important to make sure that people are aware and understand what a Census is, and why it's important," she said.

From late July, households will receive instructions on how to complete the Census. Australians can complete the form as soon as they receive instructions, provided they know where they will be on Census night.

Most people will receive a letter with instructions to complete the Census online. However, Australians can also request a paper form if they prefer.

Generally, one person per household will complete the Census, but separate forms can be requested for privacy reasons.

Some people living in remote areas of Australia, or experiencing homelessness, can complete the Census with the assistance of field staff.

The ABS has hired around 30,000 field staff to support participation. In 2021, field staff travelled more than 10 million kilometres across Australia.

Liz Allen, a demographer from the Australian National University's Centre for Social Policy Research, said: "That especially includes people in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities where ABS data collectors actually go out in force, and they ... talk to folks about the Census, what it means and to answer any relevant questions."

Information about the Census is also accessible in 25 languages, with free translation and interpreting services available for people completing the Census.

If a person is travelling within Australia on 11 August, they are still expected to complete the Census. This includes anyone travelling overnight on a long-distance train, bus, or aircraft (including red-eye flights between Perth and the east coast), and on long-haul transport vehicles that are parked or in motion.

People must include information about where they are staying or whether they are in transit.

body.en:
Lawyers for United States rapper Marshall Mathers, better known as Eminem, have filed an appeal after losing a trademark battle against Australian beach brand, Swim Shady.

The Australian Registrar of Trade Marks initially ruled in favour of Swim Shady in early July, giving the rapper's legal team until 22 July to lodge an appeal.

The rapper had launched the dispute over similarities to his alter ego 'Slim Shady' — a persona Mathers developed to give voice to his more rage-fuelled rap songs, such as his controversial 1997 Slim Shady LP album.

The Australian beach brand was founded in 2024 by former South Sydney Rabbitohs executive Jeremy Scott and partner Elizabeth Afrakoff, and makes beach shades and accessories.

Documents were lodged with the Federal Court of Australia's Victoria Registry Wednesday afternoon.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The rapper's legal team, Davies Collison Cave Law, has been contacted for comment.

Eminem's legal team claimed Mathers has used the word 'Shady' in his promotion since 1999, with the rapper launching an associated clothing brand 'Shady Limited'.

In Australia, Eminem has owned the trademarks "Shady" and "Shady Limited" for use in merchandise since 2002.

It wasn't until January 2025, however, the rapper filed for trademark rights to "Slim Shady" — a month after the launch of the Australian company.

Intellectual property law firm, Meyer West IP, acting for Swim Shady, filed a 'no-use' application for a partial removal of the rapper's trademarks, arguing that they hadn't been used in Australia for the previous three years.

The judge was not satisfied Eminem demonstrated sufficient control over his image and his business enterprises, and saw no evidence of "direct use" of his trademarks in Australia during the three-year period.

"Elizabeth and I are delighted with today's decision," founder Scott told Rolling Stone in a statement at the time.

"While this is an important milestone for Swim Shady, it is one step in the broader trade mark proceedings, and we recognise there are still matters to be resolved."

In 2017, Eminem took New Zealand's National Party to the Wellington High Court over their use of his track 'Lose Yourself' in a political campaign.

The High Court ordered the National Party to pay NZ $600,000 in damages to Eminem after using a version of the iconic guitar riff, drum beat and sparse piano melody of Lose Yourself in a re-election campaign for former Prime Minister John Key.

The battle made it to American late night talk show Last Week Tonight, where John Oliver called it "unquestionably the lamest rap beef since Lil Wayne's five year feud with William H Macy".

title.en: Minister says IS-linked doctor should 'rot in jail' after his discovery in Iraq
title.zh: 部长称与伊斯兰国有关的医生在伊拉克被发现后应该“在监狱里腐烂”

summary.en: It was assumed that pediatrician Tareq Kamleh had been killed in Syria in 2017.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The federal opposition is calling on the government to block the potential return of an Australian man who joined the so-called Islamic State militant group and was widely believed to have been killed in Syria, before being found in an Iraqi jail.

Pediatrician Tareq Kamleh, colloquially known as "Doctor Jihad" who went by the name "Abu Yusuf al-Australi", travelled to Syria in 2015 to join the terror organisation.

He was assumed to have been killed in 2017's final siege of Raqqa, the de facto capital of the self-proclaimed Islamic caliphate in Syria.

But it has since been revealed Kamleh is one-of-13 men linked to the terror group who are imprisoned in Iraq. The Australian newspaper reported on Wednesday he didn't die in the siege as his family believed.

He is believed to be among dozens of foreign fighters who were transferred from Syria to Iraq earlier this year.

When prisoners were first tranferred from Syria to Iraq earlier this year, Baghdad appealed for nations to take back their citizens and asked for financial assistance to house them in the meantime.

SBS has been unable to independently verify whether the Australian prisoners are seeking to return home.

According to Iraq's Supreme Judicial Council, Kamleh told Iraqi authorities following his transfer that he did not directly participate in combat operations but worked within what was known as the "health department" of IS, utilising his medical qualifications and experience in healthcare. 

"He provided first aid and treatment to wounded ISIS members during terrorist operations and battles against security forces," the document, seen by SBS News, states.

"The accused's activities were not limited to providing medical services. He adopted the extremist group's propaganda, advocating for terrorist activity not to be confined to conflict zone."

Iraqi judge Ali Hussein Jafat, head of the National Center for International Judicial Cooperation, said that the investigation into Kamleh was ongoing.

Labor frontbencher Clare O'Neil said she didn't want Kamleh to ever return to Australia and he should "rot in jail".

"He's obviously made a decision to join a violent death cult, and he needs to be accountable for that," she said.

But fellow senior minister Murray Watt said the government faced constitutional limitations on preventing Kamleh, an Australian citizen, from returning.

"Anyone who returns to Australia who's been part of these sorts of organisations will face the full force of the law," Senator Watt told Nine's Today program.

"We won't be providing assistance, just as we haven't provided assistance to others to come back ."

title.en: 'Truth-teller': Rebel Wilson victorious in defamation trial brought by The Deb co-star
title.zh: “真理讲述者”：瑞贝尔·威尔逊在《债务》联合主演提起的诽谤案中胜诉

summary.en: Actor Rebel Wilson won a defamation trial against her former co-star Charlotte MacInnes. MacInnes had accused Wilson of defaming her in social media posts that implied she was a liar and a sellout.
summary.zh: 演员瑞贝尔·威尔逊在一场诽谤诉讼中胜诉，该诉讼由她的前合作演员夏洛特·麦金尼斯提起。麦金尼斯曾指控威尔逊在社交媒体帖子中诽谤她，暗示她是个骗子和叛徒。

body.en:
After a blistering dispute that spanned continents and years, Hollywood A-lister Rebel Wilson has been found not to have defamed her co-star in a series of social media posts.

The Pitch Perfect star was sued by Australian actor Charlotte MacInnes, who played the lead role in Wilson's directorial debut film The Deb.

MacInnes claimed Wilson defamed her in a series of social media posts that implied she was a liar and a sellout who walked back a sexual harassment complaint to further her career.

The posts alleged the young actor confided in Wilson — and later recanted — that she felt uncomfortable when the film's co-producer Amanda Ghost asked to have a shower and a bath together.

MacInnes denied making or retracting a complaint, insisting she had not been uncomfortable when the pair shared a bath in their swimwear after Ghost suffered a medical episode in September 2023.

Two months after the conclusion of the hotly contested court fight in the Federal Court, Justice Elizabeth Raper found in favour of Wilson on Wednesday.

"MacInnes has failed to establish that the publications have caused or were likely to cause serious harm," she said.

MacInnes' barrister Sue Chrysanthou accused Wilson of a "complete revision of history" littered with dishonesty during her emphatic closing address in May.

"She is a fantastical liar who has made up terrible, terrible allegations about multiple people and her own witnesses have discredited her," she said.

But Wilson repeatedly denied accusations she fabricated the complaint or raised it for leverage during disputes with her co-producers over the film's budget and writing credit.

That was what she had been doing when she posted the stories to her 11 million followers, the Bridesmaids star said.

"I don't classify it as an attack, I classify it as telling the truth," she told the court.

Her barrister, Dauid Sibtain, said his client had "no motive to lie" about something that would endanger her film by driving a wedge between her lead actor and a producer.

Instead, he accused MacInnes of dishonestly withdrawing the complaint about Ghost to ensure her relationship with the producer continued to be fruitful.

MacInnes had received a lead role in a stage production and a six-figure record deal that were linked to Ms Ghost, he argued, and she wanted to ensure she continued to rise.

The young actor sought aggravated damages for the harm allegedly wrought by the posts, including anxiety and a period without work.

body.zh: 在一场跨越各大洲、历时数年的激烈纠纷之后，好莱坞一线明星瑞贝尔·威尔逊被发现没有在一系列社交媒体帖子中诽谤她的搭档。 这位《完美音调》的明星被澳大利亚演员夏洛特·麦金尼斯起诉，后者在威尔逊的导演处女作《黛布》中扮演主角。 麦金尼斯声称威尔逊在一系列社交媒体帖子中诽谤她，暗示她是一个骗子和出卖者，为了进一步发展自己的职业生涯，她对性骚扰投诉进行了反击。 这些帖子称，这位年轻演员向威尔逊吐露——后来又放弃了——当电影联合制片人阿曼达·幽灵要求一起洗澡时，她感到不舒服。 麦金尼斯否认提出或撤回投诉，坚称在 2023 年 9 月“幽灵”生病后，两人穿着泳衣共用浴缸时，她并没有感到不舒服。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 联邦法院这场激烈争议的法庭斗争结束两个月后，法官伊丽莎白·拉珀(Elizabeth Raper)于周三做出了对威尔逊有利的裁决。 “麦金尼斯未能证明这些出版物已经造成或可能造成严重伤害，”她说。 麦金尼斯的律师苏·克里桑托 (Sue Chrysanthou) 在五月的闭幕致辞中指责威尔逊“彻底修改历史”，充满了不诚实。 她说：“她是一个彻头彻尾的骗子，对多人做出了非常非常可怕的指控，而她自己的证人也让她名誉扫地。” 但威尔逊一再否认她捏造投诉的指控，或者在与联合制片人就电影预算和编剧功劳发生争执时提出投诉。 这位《伴娘》明星表示，当她向 1100 万粉丝发布这些故事时，她就是这么做的。 “我不把它归类为攻击，我把它归类为说实话，”她告诉法庭。 她的律师 Dauid Sibtain 表示，他的委托人“没有动机撒谎”，因为这会在她的主演和制片人之间挑拨离间，从而危及她的电影。 相反，他指责麦金尼斯不诚实地撤回了对《人鬼情未了》的投诉，以确保她与制片人的关系继续富有成效。 他认为，麦金尼斯在舞台制作中担任主角，并获得了与幽灵女士相关的六位数唱片合约，而她希望确保自己继续崛起。 这位年轻演员就据称这些帖子造成的伤害寻求加重赔偿，包括焦虑和一段时间没有工作。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: This story reminds us that while falsehoods can spread rapidly, truth ultimately has enduring power. In a world often quick to judge based on fleeting social media posts, the legal process here affirmed the lasting nature of truth over temporary accusations. Yahweh's word assures us that truthful lips endure, even when challenged.
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，虽然谎言可能迅速传播，但真理最终拥有持久的力量。在一个常常根据短暂的社交媒体帖子迅速做出判断的世界里，这次法律程序肯定了真理相对于暂时指控的持久性。雅伟的话语向我们保证，诚实的嘴唇必存到永远，即使受到挑战。

verse.textEn: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
